root_cause.text: The Xen SCSI backend driver (`drivers/xen/xen-scsiback.c`) allocates the per-device `struct vscsiblk_info` in `scsiback_probe()` but `scsiback_remove()` failed to free that object, causing a memory leak on device removal and in probe error paths.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says “Memory allocated for struct vscsiblk_info in scsiback_probe() is not freed in scsiback_remove()”; the patch fixes this by adding `kfree(info);` at the end of `scsiback_remove()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Xen SCSI backend driver (`drivers/xen/xen-scsiback.c`) allocates the per-device `struct vscsiblk_info` in `scsiback_probe()` but `scsiback_remove()` failed to free that object, causing a memory leak on device removal and in probe error paths.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says “Memory allocated for struct vscsiblk_info in scsiback_probe() is not freed in scsiback_remove()”; the patch fixes this by adding `kfree(info);` at the end of `scsiback_remove()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the scsiback private data during device removal to fix a memory leak.
intent_record.what: In `scsiback_remove(struct xenbus_device *dev)`, a new `kfree(info);` call was added immediately after `dev_set_drvdata(&dev->dev, NULL);`.
intent_record.how: When the xenbus device is removed, the `info` structure is now explicitly freed instead of only being detached from the device, preventing a memory leak during driver teardown.

grouping_result.intent: Free the scsiback private data during device removal to fix a memory leak.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it frees the per-device scsiback private data on removal, fixing the memory leak caused by scsiback_remove() not releasing the allocated vscsiblk_info.

candidates.rationale: This is the cleanup performed in scsiback_remove(), but the pre-fix code stopped here without freeing the per-device private struct vscsiblk_info allocated in probe, so the device-specific memory remained leaked on removal.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the last cleanup statement in scsiback_remove() before the missing free of the per-device struct vscsiblk_info. Because the function stopped after shrinking the page cache and did not release the allocated private device object, the allocation made in probe leaked on device removal.

commit ca33479cc7be2c9b5f8be078c8bf3ac26b7d6186
Author: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Date:   Mon Dec 7 08:31:22 2020 +0100

    xen: add helpers for caching grant mapping pages
    
    Instead of having similar helpers in multiple backend drivers use
    common helpers for caching pages allocated via gnttab_alloc_pages().
    
    Make use of those helpers in blkback and scsiback.
    
    Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 5.9
    Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
    Reviewed-by:
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff removes the old global free-page list logic and replaces it with per-device cache helpers. In particular, `scsiback_probe()` now initializes `info->free_pages` with `gnttab_page_cache_init(&info->free_pages);`, and `scsiback_remove()` now explicitly tears it down with `gnttab_page_cache_shrink(&info->free_pages, 0);`. This addresses the root cause of leaking per-device allocation state on removal. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause—`struct vscsiblk_info` being allocated in probe but not freed in remove—is not shown here, and the diff does not indicate that bug; instead, it shows cleanup being added for the page cache associated with the device.
